**Blocker for the browser picker:** in Safari, File > Open model did not let the user open any file. The app loaded fine ("no theme folder found beside the exe - the built-in themes stand" was the only status line), but no model came in and no error was shown. Safari is the browser most likely to block a file chooser not opened directly from the user's click (it requires transient user activation), so this is probably the main thing the async picker has to handle. Please investigate and either fix it or show a clear message in Safari. A silent no-op is the failure the check was written to catch.

Side note: on a fresh page, both Safari and Chrome show "no theme folder found beside the exe - the built-in themes stand" in the status line. In the browser build that wording ("exe") is misleading; consider suppressing it on wasm.

Taken over from SKULL (its budget is out for today) with the user's OK, to keep it moving: M5 works the Safari File > Open fix from the hand check above. SKULL: please check the PR before resuming it tomorrow; plain pushes only, nothing force-pushed.

**Safari fix pushed - head 0dd7eebc** (taken over from SKULL with the user's OK). Answers the hand check above.

**Root cause.** eframe 0.36.2 runs the app's frame inside its `pointerup` listener (`web/events.rs`, `install_pointerup` calls `runner.logic()` there; its own comment says Safari allows certain things only "on user action, such as a click"). The ribbon queued `OpenModelDialog` in that frame, but `WebShell::ui` drains the queue at the **start of the next frame**, which eframe runs from `requestAnimationFrame`. Chrome and Brave still opened the chooser there: their transient activation is a timed window that outlasts the click (MDN, "User activation": transient activation "expires after a timeout"). Safari opens a file chooser only while the user's input event is being handled and ignores `input.click()` elsewhere without an error, which is the silent no-op you saw.

**Fix.**
- `State::run_click_actions(in_click)` (`crates/ui/src/state_picked.rs`): at the end of the frame that saw a pointer release (the one eframe runs inside `pointerup`), the queue runs at once if it holds an action that may open a chooser: Open model, Open project, and the unsaved-changes answer that lets a held Open project go on. `input.click()` therefore runs inside the user's click. The web shell calls it after the 3D pass (`shell_web.rs`).
- The hidden `<input type=file>` is attached to the page with `display:none` and removed when replaced. This is MDN's "Using files from web applications" pattern: a hidden input whose `click()` runs from a click handler. A detached input is no longer relied on.
- The Cmd/Ctrl+O shortcut is still handed over on a later frame (eframe's keydown listener does not run the frame). It still tries, which works in Chrome. The status line then reads "choose a model to import… if no file chooser opened, this browser (Safari) opens one only from a click - click File > Model instead of the shortcut", so it is never silent.
- The browser build starts "ready" instead of "no theme folder found beside the exe" (`theme_dir::startup_status`).
- Merged upstream/main (f84059c9). #1431 had refused Open model / Open project in the browser "until the browser file picker (#31)". This PR is that picker, so those two refusals are lifted, and the #1431 tests now assert the cells are live.

**Considered and dropped** (recorded in `docs/decisions/31-wasm-file-picker.md`):
- A "Choose file…" overlay for every browser. It adds a second click in Chrome.
- Sniffing the user agent for Safari.
- `navigator.userActivation` or `window.event` to detect the refusal. MDN marks `window.event` deprecated, and a timed activation can still be refused by WebKit's file input.

**Sources:** MDN "User activation"; MDN "Using files from web applications" (hidden input + `click()`); MDN `Window.event`; eframe 0.36.2 `src/web/events.rs` (`install_pointerup`, `on_keydown`).
